curriculum.lesson_evidence: Safe rolling starts with simple, low-risk rolls on a mat, such as a log roll (body straight, rolling sideways) and an egg roll (curled up and rocking). Tuck rolls and forward rolls are taught by a teacher or coach with mats and supervision. For safe jumping and landing, bend the knees, land on the balls of the feet, keep feet about shoulder-width apart, arms forward and chest up. Never jump from high places. Stop if you feel pain or dizziness or someone is in the way.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A child jumps off a high step and lands with straight legs. Write what the problem is and a safer way.

FEEDBACK
Straight legs and a high drop send a lot of force into the joints. Jump only from a low, flat place, bend the knees on landing and land on the balls of the feet with arms forward.

WATCH FOR
Thinking a big jump from a high place is better. A good landing is soft and controlled, and height increases risk.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
On a mat or soft grass with an adult nearby, practise a log roll, an egg roll and five low jumps with soft landings. Record a technique score from 1 to 3 for each (shape, control, landing). Use cue words and stop if anything hurts.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example on a mat. Log roll: lie straight with arms overhead and roll sideways, keeping the body in a line. Egg roll: curl into a ball and rock gently from side to side. Jump and land: bend the knees, jump up, land on the balls of the feet with knees bent and arms forward, then hold for 2 seconds. Safety: a clear space, a mat and an adult nearby.

TRY FIRST
A child jumps off a high step and lands with straight legs. Write what the problem is and a safer way.

FEEDBACK
Straight legs and a high drop send a lot of force into the joints. Jump only from a low, flat place, bend the knees on landing and land on the balls of the feet with arms forward.

For safe jumping and landing, bend the knees, land on the balls of the feet, keep feet about shoulder-width apart, arms forward and chest up. Never jump from high places. Stop if you feel pain or dizziness or someone is in the way.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.

teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new situation.
teaching.model: Safe rolling starts with simple, low-risk rolls on a mat, such as a log roll (body straight, rolling sideways) and an egg roll (curled up and rocking). Tuck rolls and forward rolls are taught by a teacher or coach with mats and supervision. For safe jumping and landing, bend the knees, land on the balls of the feet, keep feet about shoulder-width apart, arms forward and chest up. Never jump from high places. Stop if you feel pain or dizziness or someone is in the way. Now choose a different situation to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
